root_cause.text: Missing NULL pointer checks before calling xfarray_destroy and xfblob_destroy in XFS repair cleanup functions, which can lead to a NULL pointer dereference or double-free when the pointer was never allocated or after a previous cleanup.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds conditional checks (if (ptr)) before each destructor call and sets the pointer to NULL after destruction in multiple files (agheader_repair.c, attr_repair.c, dir_repair.c, dirtree.c, nlinks.c). The commit message states "only call xf{array,blob}_destroy if we have a valid pointer", and the CVE description confirms the same vulnerability. The Fixes tag points to commit ab97f4b1c03075 ("xfs: repair AGI unlinked inode bucket lists") as the origin of the flawed pattern.

    Reviewed-by: Christoph Hellwig <hch@lst.de>

diff --git a/fs/xfs/scrub/agheader_repair.c b/fs/xfs/scrub/agheader_repair.c
index d210bd7d5eb1..0dbc484b182f 100644
--- a/fs/xfs/scr
bic_trace_step.reason: In the newly added cleanup function xrep_agi_buf_cleanup (line 821-827), xfarray_destroy is called on ragi->iunlink_prev and ragi->iunlink_next without NULL checks.
